content: The classification of diabetes, as defined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes the following categories: 1. Type 1 Diabetes: This form of diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, which are responsible for producing insulin. The destruction of these cells typically leads to an absolute deficiency of insulin in the body. 2. Type 2 Diabetes: This type is frequently associated with insulin resistance, where the body's cells do not respond effectively to insulin. Over time, there is also a progressive decline in the ability of the pancreas to secrete insulin adequately. 3. Other Specific Types of Diabetes: These include less common forms of diabetes such as neonatal diabetes, which occurs in newborns, and maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY), which is a monogenic form of diabetes that typically presents in adolescence or early adulthood. Additionally, diabetes can result from pancreatic diseases or as a side effect of certain medications.
